title: How to organize the sink and dishwashing zone | Kitchen
description:
The washing point for dishes, hands, and produce, and the place the whole kitchen resets from.

This is the Sink and Dishwashing Zone in the Kitchen. About 30-45 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
An empty sink with a dry basin and a wiped drain flange. One brush and one sponge standing upright where they drain rather than lying in a puddle. The drying rack either empty or holding only what is still wet. Under the sink, a single tray holding dish soap, dishwasher tablets, and one all-purpose cleaner, with the pipes visible around them.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Pull everything out from under the sink and line it up on the floor.
Straighten: Soap and brush live in a caddy you can lift with one wet hand, so wiping under them takes no planning.
Shine: The sponge is the dirtiest object in the room: wring it out and stand it on edge after every wash, and retire
Safety: Never store bleach beside an ammonia or toilet cleaner under this sink, and never combine them in the basin; k
Standardize: Write the empty-sink standard on a card taped inside the cabinet door: dishes in the machine or washed, basin
Sustain: The last thing before the kitchen light goes off, the sink gets emptied and the basin gets wiped dry.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Empty sink, dry basin, one brush and one sponge standing, cleaners on one tray with the plumbing visible.
